A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ECG foundation-model benchmark and ECG-CPC model. Text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning, frozen-feature, linear-evaluation, and label-efficiency experiments, with aggregate and per-label results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds computational profiling, learning-rate ablations, Mamba comparisons, representation analyses, and alternative-metric results.

M1.justification: ECG-CPC's architecture, CPC objective, downstream heads, and fine-tuning procedure are retained (Section 3.3; Appendix A.2). Table 1 changes MERL's architecture label from Transformer to CNN, but both versions already specify the ResNet18 encoder; this is a documentation correction.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 12 datasets, 26 clinical tasks, and seven task categories. The dataset inventory in v1 Table 3 matches v2 Table 2. Added analyses use retained datasets and prediction tasks without introducing new populations or input scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix A.8 and Table 34 add Mamba-1 and Mamba-2 alongside S4 and Net1D in supervised backbone comparisons on PTB-XL, EchoNext, and CPSC-Extra. This is a focused extension; the main eight-FM and two-baseline comparison remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce CKA evaluation on 2,500 PTB-XL samples, computational profiling with specified hardware and batch sizes, learning-rate controls, and specificity/F1 evaluation at sensitivity 0.8 (Appendices A.6–A.10). Table 1 also revises ECG-FM's reported pretraining sample count from 2.5M to 1.5M, without establishing retraining.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends the analyses with layer-dependent learning-rate ablations, supervised backbone comparisons, intra-model and inter-model CKA, computational-efficiency measurements, and agreement between AUROC and threshold-dependent metrics. The earlier scaling and per-label analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 3.3 newly states that no global random seed is fixed. Both versions retain 1,000 test-set bootstrap iterations and significance judgments based on 95% confidence intervals for paired performance differences. No increase in repeated training runs is reported.

E6.justification: Matched aggregate scores, rankings, per-label results, and scaling fits are unchanged. v2 adds substantial results from the new analyses: for example, Table 33 reports PTB-XL AUROC of 0.940 versus 0.779 for ECG-JEPA with versus without layer-dependent learning rates, while Figure 6 reports differing AUROC and F1 rankings. These are added findings, not improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: The scaling-law expression and label-efficiency ratio are retained. The new CKA, profiling, and metric comparisons are empirical analyses; no substantive mathematical definitions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions shift from heterogeneous benchmark performance and a promising compact model to the stronger claim that architecture matters more than scale. Divergent representations despite similar performance become a core contribution. The headline label-efficiency range changes from 2.5–9× to 3.3–9× despite unchanged scaling tables.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations involving representational redundancy and bottlenecks, SSM inductive biases, scaling slopes versus performance ceilings, and the clinical meaning of metric agreement. It also qualifies learning-rate benefits by architecture and expands discussion of pretraining confounds and evaluating released checkpoints. Existing in-distribution and multitask limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents batch size 64, 100 training epochs, signal-encoder-only use for multimodal models, and the single-query attention head. It also supplies Mamba configurations and profiling conditions. These extend reproducibility information without establishing changes to the retained experiments; the code and checkpoint access location remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused references and positioning around foundation-model definitions, biomedical FMs, CKA, AUROC, and S4 versus newer Mamba models. It removes Dehghani's efficiency citation while retaining the main benchmarking background. Several other reference changes are publication updates for existing works.

P1.justification: The abstract, research-gap paragraph, and contribution statement are substantially rewritten around architecture, efficiency, and representation questions. Results are reorganized, methodology and discussion explanations expand, and FM terminology is standardized throughout. This materially changes the narrative beyond simply appending experiments.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned, and the radar plots are rearranged with reversed radial ranking direction and removal of the S4 panel. The abbreviated main-text performance table disappears while full appendix tables remain. New CKA heatmaps, metric bar charts, and Tables 32–34 substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 improves empirical support and reproducibility through explicit training details, learning-rate controls, resource measurements, and alternative-metric checks. These make the retained benchmark more useful. The net gain is limited by the stronger architecture-over-scale conclusion despite acknowledged pretraining confounds, and an unexplained inconsistency: Table 34 reports Net1D EchoNext/CPSC-Extra scores of 0.818/0.803, whereas retained Table 3 gives 0.803/0.818. The additions strengthen documentation and supporting evidence more clearly than the broader conclusions.
